summary: The super admin role is merged into admin: admins now hold every former super admin ability, with sensitive changes behind a re-confirmed sign-in. The public repository also gains its licence, Code of Conduct, security, contributing and support files.
detailed_changes: Merged the super admin role into admin. Former super admins sign in as admin, and their stored role and audit entries were converted, with a snapshot kept for rollback (#714, #715, #724).
Integration keys, mail sending settings and Mailgun webhook and tracking changes now need an admin who re-confirmed their sign-in in the last five minutes; staff are refused (#716).
Admins can lock, unlock, sign out, reset, edit, delete or demote other admins after re-confirming their sign-in, never their own account, and the last unlocked admin is always kept (#717, #720).
Testing an integration connection now needs a recent sign-in too (#742).
Scheduled publishing, integration alerts, campaign alerts, author lists, API token owners and the Ghost importer use admins (#718).
Removed super admin from the staff and admin screens and the local role preview (#719, #722).
Wrote a security review of the wider admin rights into the threat model, with a recommendation to keep two-factor sign-in on for every admin (#720).
Added a runbook for retiring the old Cloudron super admin group without anyone losing access (#723).
Added the AGPL-3.0 licence, Code of Conduct, security policy, contributing and support guides, Discussion forms and a refreshed README (#727).
affected_areas: User groups affected: staff and admins
Internal impact: one admin role, re-confirmed sign-in for sensitive changes, Cloudron group change, repository licence and community files
